title: Lease-based KV Windowing and NCCL Burst Coalescing to Reduce Microcollective Overhead
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce lease-based KV entries and a windowed all-reduce coalescer that reduces small collective frequency, plus NCCL burst coalescing knobs and scheduler integration. Improves small-sequence TP latency and throughput with bounded added latency.
body:
Context: small, high-QPS microbatches and continuous batching expose a pathological pattern in tensor-parallel workflows where frequent KV cache evictions and many small all-reduce/NCCL calls dominate CPU/GPU scheduling overhead and NCCL latency.
Motivation: reduce the number of fine-grained collectives without compromising worst-case latency or cache correctness. This PR implements a lease-based KV windowing mechanism coupled with a windowed all-reduce coalescer and targeted NCCL burst/coalesce tuning.
Design summary: 1) KV Lease Manager: new lease semantics for KV entries used by continuing prefix/cache windows. A lease gives the runtime a bounded period (configurable default 8ms) during which an entry is eligible for delayed eviction to allow cross-microbatch coalescing. Leases are lightweight and per-peer (not global) to preserve correctness for partial shard eviction.
2) Windowed AllReduce Coalescer: the TP collective path buffers small tensor collectives that are marked coalescible into a single batched all-reduce according to a window (max_count=4, max_wait=6ms). Windows are sized by token-size heuristics and KV lease membership; the algorithm guarantees deterministic ordering and fallback to immediate dispatch if window thresholds are exceeded.
3) NCCL burst/coalescing knobs: a small set of NCCL params and stream scheduling adjustments (burst_coalesce=true, async_stream_batch=2) that increase the effective coalescing of adjacent launches while keeping occupancy constraints. These knobs are guarded behind runtime detection and can be disabled per-cluster.
4) Scheduler integration: the launch scheduler is extended to be window-aware: it pre-reserves streams and defers kernel launch until window closure for coalescible tensors. This includes safety gates for latency-sensitive requests (pin request tag to bypass).
Benchmarks (8xA100, 16 TP ranks, small sequence length 32, real prompt mix):
- Median token tail latency reduced by 18% (from 42.5ms -> 34.9ms) for the small-seq microbatch workload.
- Aggregate throughput improved by 27% for 32-token steady-state streams.
- NCCL call count reduced by 42% for the workload mix; average NCCL call size increased ~2.4x.
- KV eviction churn decreased 60% due to leases, reducing memory churn and CPU GC spikes.
Implementation notes:
- New files: src/runtime/tp/collectives/windowed_allreduce.cpp/.h, src/runtime/kv/lease_manager.cpp/.h, src/runtime/scheduler/window_coordinator.cpp/.h, src/runtime/nccl/nccl_tuner.cpp (tuning knobs), integration stubs in continuous_batcher.cc.
- Exposed two runtime knobs: redwood.runtime.kv_lease_ms and redwood.runtime.tp_window_ms; both default conservative values.
- Backwards-compatible: if leases/windowing disabled, behavior is identical to prior code path.
- Tests: added unit tests and a micro-benchmark harness under benchmarks/perf/windowed_allreduce_bench.py.
Checklist:
- [x] Design doc (docs/rfcs/lease-kv-windowing.md)
- [x] Unit tests for lease semantics and coalescer
- [x] Integration perf harness and baseline numbers
- [x] Runtime knobs & gating
- [x] CI green
- [x] Benchmarks added and reviewed
Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: increased worst-case latency for extremely latency-sensitive single-request flows. Mitigation: pinning tag bypasses windowing; window defaults are conservative and subject to rollout.
- Risk: interactions with Dedicated autoscaler jitter. Mitigation: disabled by default on Dedicated until canary complete.
Rollout plan: staged canary on internal perf cluster -> 10% customer canary with metrics tracking (KV eviction rate, NCCL call count, token latency) -> global release.
Related work: builds on prior comm-coalescing work (see ENG-2237) and NCCL pacing experiments in nccl_tuner. This PR is intentionally conservative with defaults to avoid user-facing latency regressions.
